A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AMCN research. Their text, equations, seven figures, four tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched reliably across layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original AMCN detection results, component ablations, parameter analyses, and qualitative examples in Section 4. These qualify independently of the baseline results attributed to other works.

after.justification: V2 retains the original AMCN experiments and analyses in Section 4, including the proposed method’s results in Table 1 and ablations in Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same three prompt types, class-dependent thresholds, distribution updates, normalization components, and training losses. No algorithmic or architectural component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1k as ID data and Texture, Places, SUN, and iNaturalist as OOD evaluation data. No evaluated task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains KNN, ViM, ODIN, NPOS, GL-MCM, MCM, SeTAR, CoOp, LoCoOp, and SCT in the same comparisons. Figure 1 also retains NPOS and PALM. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same dataset-selection procedure, 1/2/4/8/16-shot settings, CLIP-ViT-B/16 backbone, training settings, and FPR95/AUROC metrics. The ablation controls and encoder comparisons are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the module, prompt-type, and threshold ablations in Tables 2–4; loss-weight sensitivity in Figure 5; prompt-count and encoder analyses in Figure 7; and Places examples in Figure 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical entries, and the plotted results and qualitative examples match. For example, AMCN’s one-shot Texture FPR95/AUROC remains 39.16/89.88, and its eight-shot result remains 38.31/93.43.

T1.justification: The problem definitions and Equations (1)–(18) are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same unit-hypersphere argument and Equations (19)–(22), with no added or revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive prompts, class-diversity modeling, and superior few-shot OOD detection performance.

C2.justification: The explanations linking performance to background handling, prompt design, and class diversity remain unchanged. Appendix B preserves the same discussion of semantic and contextual variability, collection bias, and generalization difficulties.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 supplies the same hyperparameters, AdamW optimizer, learning rate, batch size, token length, and epoch count. Both PDFs contain the same GitHub link and dataset-split references, with no additional reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands the cited literature through dozens of introductory references, including EOOD and works on video grounding, point clouds, and quantum multiplication. It removes the earlier uncertainty-guided appearance-motion action-detection reference. Section 2’s comparative discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction’s citation block expands substantially, two unresolved citation placeholders disappear, and citation-year suffixes change. The surrounding prose, section sequence, terminology, and appendix wording remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 move from pages 2 and 3 to pages 3 and 4; Figure 3 and Table 4 change columns. The expanded bibliography causes further reflow, while figure contents, table structures, legends, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Removing the unresolved citation placeholders provides a small editorial benefit. However, v2 introduces a lengthy introductory citation block without explaining its connections, including a quantum-multiplication reference, and duplicates the same temporal-grounding paper as Fang et al. (2025g, 2025h). These changes modestly reduce readability and bibliographic precision; the scientific content and appendices remain unchanged.
